headline: Quarter beats own targets, but full-year outlook cut
summary_short: FMC's Q2 2026 revenue was $867.1M, down 17% y/y (+14.3% q/q), with a GAAP net loss of $186.6M (diluted EPS -$1.49) and Adjusted EBITDA of $153M — above the high end of prior guidance — even as the company cut full-year 2026 revenue, EBITDA and EPS guidance.
summary_long: Revenue fell 17% y/y to $867.1M (20% ex-India) as a 10% volume decline — lower diamide partner orders and weak North America legacy demand — combined with 7% price erosion, partly offset by a 2% FX tailwind; the India divestiture cut another 5 points. GAAP net loss widened to $186.6M on higher restructuring charges ($222.3M vs $36.7M) and interest expense, though Adjusted EBITDA of $153M beat the high end of prior guidance and Adjusted EPS was $0.26. Cash from operations rose to $363M, aided by a $200M rimisoxafen licensing payment. FMC cut full-year revenue, EBITDA and EPS guidance, citing a tougher demand environment, while raising free-cash-flow guidance.

drivers.explanation: Volumes fell 10% on lower diamide partner orders and weaker North America legacy-product demand; price fell 7% on core-product pressure and Rynaxypyr pricing actions; FX added 2%; the India divestiture cut another 5 points.
Restructuring and other charges rose to $222.3M from $36.7M, driven mainly by Project Foundation non-cash asset write-offs and accelerated depreciation tied to planned exits of production activities.
Lower price and volume were partially offset by favorable costs and a moderate FX tailwind.
GAAP net loss widened on lower sales, higher restructuring costs, and higher interest expense, per the release.
Cash from operations rose $297M y/y, including a $200M upfront payment from Corteva under the rimisoxafen licensing agreement.
Not directly explained; consistent with trailing-twelve-month GAAP net losses attributable to stockholders of about $2.76B shown in the release's own ROIC reconciliation table.

CEO Pierre Brondeau said the India, Newark and Tessenderlo actions strengthened FMC's financial footing; the strategic review is now concluded and focus shifts to competitiveness and the technology portfolio.
